record.paper_title: Open questions for strongly interacting Fermi gases with zero-range interactions
record.original_question: In a weakly polarized pair-condensed Fermi gas, where the excess majority-spin fermions appear as gapped fermionic quasiparticles χ and the low-energy sound quanta are phonons φ, what are the correct low-energy φ–χ and χ–χ interactions? In particular, what is the correct low-energy φ–χ scattering amplitude, given that existing calculations disagree?

evidence.quote: The question then arises of the φ−χ and of the χ−χ interactions; in particular, disagreement persists over the expression of the low-energy φ − χ scattering amplitude (references [64] and [65] differ).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a three-dimensional pair-condensed (BCS-BEC crossover) Fermi gas of two spin species with a small population imbalance. In the weakly polarized regime, the excess majority-spin fermions form a dilute population of gapped fermionic quasiparticles, denoted χ, while the low-energy collective excitations of the paired condensate are gapless phonons, denoted φ, with a linear dispersion at long wavelength.

Working within a low-energy effective field theory built from the order-parameter (phonon) field and the gapped Bogoliubov quasiparticle field on top of the BCS ground state, derive the correct low-energy effective interactions between these degrees of freedom, namely:

(i) the φ–χ coupling vertex and the resulting on-shell phonon–quasiparticle scattering amplitude in the limit of small phonon momentum and quasiparticle momentum near the gap minimum, and

(ii) the χ–χ effective interaction (induced direct quasiparticle–quasiparticle scattering, including phonon-mediated contributions).

In particular, determine the unambiguous expression for the leading low-energy φ–χ scattering amplitude as a function of the equation-of-state parameters of the unpolarized superfluid (e.g., the chemical potential, sound velocity, and gap, together with their derivatives with respect to density), reconciling the conflicting results that have appeared in the literature.

artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any publication that resolves the discrepancy between existing computations of the low-energy phonon–quasiparticle scattering amplitude in a weakly polarized pair-condensed Fermi gas. The problem is presented as an open question with conflicting results in the literature, and no resolution was located. Status is therefore taken as open.

status_evidence.title: Collisional Properties of a Polarized Fermi Gas with Resonant Interactions
status_evidence.snippet: Highly polarized mixtures of atomic Fermi gases constitute a novel Fermi liquid; thermodynamic properties may be used to calculate quasiparticle scattering amplitudes even when the interaction is resonant.
status_evidence.claim: Quasiparticle scattering amplitudes in polarized resonant Fermi gases remain an active area of research without a single agreed-upon low-energy expression.

status_evidence.title: Exact Quasiparticle Properties of a Heavy Polaron in BCS Fermi Superfluids
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of quasiparticle interactions with phonons in BCS Fermi superfluids continue, indicating the topic remains under active theoretical investigation.
status_evidence.claim: Recent works continue to investigate phonon–quasiparticle interactions in BCS superfluids, consistent with the question being unresolved.
